paper.title_en: The Activation Detectors Application for Calibration of Intensity Sensors of Extracted Intermediate-Energy Light Ion Beams at Accelerators
paper.abstract_en: A novel technique for the absolute calibration of ionization chambers measuring the intensity of extracted carbon ion beams in the 400-450 MeV/nucleon energy range using activation detectors has been proposed at the Institute for High Energy Physics of the National Research Center "Kurchatov Institute". A radiometric facility operating on the gamma-gamma coincidence principle, an activation detector made of pure carbon with a natural isotope mixture, and the $^{12}$C($^{12}$C, X)$^{11}$C reaction are used. This study examines the prerequisites for developing this technique, provides a general description, and describes the process of a plane-parallel ionization chamber calibration during its regular operation at the experimental Radiobiological Stand of the U-70 Accelerator Complex at the IHEP, NRC "Kurchatov Institute".
